messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased tail latency detected on kv-cache shards (region-us-west-2). p95 -> 280ms (+120ms), p99 -> 1.8s (+900ms). Streaming stalls observed for ~3m. Alerts: kv-cache.evictions.rate, streaming.tail.stalls.count. Page sent to #eng-oncall.

maria: acked. I'm on it. pinging SRE and infra. Initial customer impact: several hosted API customers reporting streaming stalls and slow completions; no widespread 5xx spike yet. :thinking_face:

devon: diving into dashboards now — linking live graphs: https://dashboards.internal/datadog/abc123 (streaming latency heatmap + per-shard eviction rate). Looks like eviction spikes correlate with increased prefill queue size on a subset of shards.

elena: I see KV slab fragmentation on node-set gpu-pool-8-*. Prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill threads are queuing up while decode workers are saturated. That causes long tail for new streaming sessions that need prefill KV entries.

maria: good find. Can we confirm it's fragmentation (many small free blocks) vs overall memory pressure? Which metric shows slab utilization? devon?

devon: slab.free_blocks_ratio on affected shards jumped from 0.12 -> 0.52 around 12:02 UTC. total_free_memory is not critically low, but allocation churn is high. Eviction rate doubled in 2m window. p99 for streaming stalls aligns with eviction peaks.

ryan: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase prefetched-kv-limit per request to reduce concurrent prefill ops; 2) divert streaming traffic for high-latency model routes to warm pool (dedicated smaller cache with reserved capacity); 3) throttle prefill frequency to favor decode path. Which is lowest-risk to push now?

elena: 3) throttle prefill frequency is safest — reduces pressure on cache alloc path immediately. We can flip a feature-flag: `kv.prefill.max_concurrency` from 200 -> 50. Patch is a config change on the control plane.

maria: agree, do 3) first. devon, can you apply the flag in staging-ish then prod rollout? Also, add a temporary auto-eviction bump: `kv.eviction.bias=0.7` to prefer freeing larger spans.

devon: applying prefill throttle now. Command:
```
# set feature-flag
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/flags -d '{"flag":"kv.prefill.max_concurrency","value":50}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"
```
Rolling to prod in 2 mins. Will monitor.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout of flag kv.prefill.max_concurrency=50 to clusters: gpu-pool-8, gpu-pool-9. Rollout id: roll-69500-01. Watch: https://deploys.internal/rolls/roll-69500-01

maria: while that's rolling, Elena — can you backfill a short-lived config bump to decode worker threads? e.g. `decoder.worker_count += 2` for the affected nodes. That should shave a chunk of p99.

elena: on it. Patching node pool config now. Using runbook section "decode-thread-burst". ETA 90s.

sre-oncall: I've scaled up a couple of warm pool instances as a stopgap: 3 x t4g-large equivalents in us-west-2. Routing rule applied to move 10% of streaming traffic for large models to warm pool. If stalls persist we can increase to 25%.

maria: confirm: we've applied prefill throttle, bumped decode threads, and routed subset to warm pool. devon, any signal yet?

devon: initial signal: eviction.rate down ~30% on impacted shards; p99 streaming latency back to ~650ms (from 1.8s). p95 stable at ~200-250ms. Streaming stall count decreased but not zero.

product-ops: heads up — two enterprise customers (acme-corp, finlytics) reported increased latency. We should send preliminary notification if degradation persists >30m. Are we at that point?

maria: Not yet, but we'll monitor. I'll prepare a short status to send if we cross 15m more with p99>600ms. @product-ops hold tight.

ryan: next steps: schedule a rolling GC+slab-compact on affected node-set during off-peak to reclaim fragmentation. That is higher risk (short restarts), so do as a planned mitigation after immediate measures.

elena: agreed. I'll run a compact on a single shard as a canary after we stabilize. Runbook: `kv-slab-compact --shard gpu-pool-8-a --dry-run` then actual. Will coordinate window.

devon: deploy-bot reports rollout successful on all clusters. Rollout logs: "kv.prefill.max_concurrency updated". Observability link: https://dashboards.internal/datadog/roll-69500-01

ops-bot: infra-bot: warm-pool scaling and routing applied. 10% traffic moved. No errors from routing layer.

maria: summary for handoff -> Next oncall (Elena will remain SRE point, Ryan will lead infra changes):
- what: p99 streaming latency spike caused by KV cache slab fragmentation + prefill vs decode imbalance
- impact: intermittent streaming stalls, p99 peaked ~1.8s, some customer-reported slow streams; no mass 5xx
- mitigations applied: prefill concurrency throttled (50), decode worker count +2, warm-pool routing (10%), scaled warm nodes x3
- observed effect: eviction rate -30%, p99 -> ~650ms, stall count decreased
- followups: scheduled slab-compact canary, investigate root cause of sudden fragmentation (workload shift? mem alloc pattern), create incident ticket and postmortem (owner: maria)
- customer comms: product-ops to draft preliminary notice if not resolved in 15m

elena: I'll take the handoff. Leaving a note: if p99 stays >700ms for additional 10m, escalate to full shard drain + compact and inform SRE lead.

maria: thanks all. moving to watch. I'll update thread in 5m or on further changes.

devon: metrics update (12:09 UTC): p99 630ms, p95 210ms, eviction.rate trending down. Keeping dashboards pinned.

sre-oncall: creating incident CI-6950012345 in tracker with timeline + runbook links.

product-ops: standing by for comms. I'll prepare a short blurb with affected endpoints and mitigation steps. Will wait for your go, Maria.

maria: go ahead and draft; hold sending until I review. tagging this for postmortem follow-up. :memo:

elena: handing off fully to next rotation at 12:12 UTC. All mitigations in place. If anything new, ping #eng-oncall. "handoff: stabilized, monitor, compact planned".

maria: thanks Elena. thread locked to oncall team. Watchlist: acme-corp, finlytics. Last message for handoff timestamp: 6950012678.
